claims.text: The baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating has a coarse, inhomogeneous distribution of Cu-rich precipitates.
The baseline coating has a predominantly single-phase matrix.
A controlled post-deposition heat treatment will refine the size distribution of Cu-rich precipitates.
A controlled post-deposition heat treatment will make the spatial distribution of Cu-rich precipitates more uniform.
Smaller Cu-rich precipitates impede dislocation motion in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
A uniform spatial distribution of Cu-rich precipitates impedes dislocation motion in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Refined Cu-rich precipitates delay localized plastic deformation during sliding.
Refined Cu-rich precipitates delay dynamic recrystallization during sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and delayed localized plastic deformation enhance the coating's wear resistance.
The heat-treated coating will have a lower high-temperature wear rate than the baseline coating.
The heat-treated coating will exhibit less-pronounced surface plastic-deformation zones than the baseline coating during high-temperature sliding.
The predicted improvements should occur above approximately 300 °C under service-representative loads and sliding conditions.
Diffusion and dynamic-recovery mechanisms are activated in the stated high-temperature regime.
The benefits of precipitate refinement may not be significant at lower temperatures.
